title: Microsoft Viva: targeted audience surveys in the Copilot Dashboard
summary: The briefing's rollout, default, audience protections and controls are supported by Microsoft's notice and current documentation. Minor corrections should finish the policy-creation path, acknowledge differing licensing documentation and identify the checklist controls missing from the table.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft documents full Viva Pulse functionality for users with a Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Users with a Microsoft Copilot license have access to the full functionality of Viva Pulse to gather real-time feedback from their teams.
claims.fix: After this sentence add: 'Microsoft documentation differs: the general Viva Pulse licensing requirements page lists Viva Suite, Viva Workplace Analytics and Employee Feedback, Viva Glint and the Viva Pulse Admin-led Trial for the full premium experience, but does not list Microsoft Copilot. The in-app setup page also says Copilot-only subscriptions do not provide customization, notification, Viva resources or delegation administration.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/pulse/get-started/licensing-requirements and https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/pulse/setup-admin-access/set-up-in-app-pulse-experience.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Dashboard integration requires Viva Suite, Viva Workplace Analytics and Employee Feedback, Viva Glint or Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: To integrate Pulse survey results into the Copilot Dashboard, you must have at least one of the following subscription licenses: Viva Suite; Viva Workplace Analytics and Employee Feedback; Viva Glint; Microsoft Copilot

claims.claim: Under the Microsoft Copilot subscription, Copilot impact template results are automatically shared to the Copilot Dashboard.
claims.quote: As part of this subscription, Viva Pulse survey results for the Copilot impact template are automatically shared to the Microsoft Copilot Dashboard

claims.claim: The documented Viva feature access management controls are not available in GCC High or DoD.
claims.quote: The access controls described in this document aren't available in GCC-High or DoD.

claims.claim: The policy-creation route is Microsoft 365 admin center > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy.
claims.quote: select Viva from the settings menu. Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. Select Create a policy. Name the policy and select the app and feature ... Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off
claims.fix: Extend the path to 'Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > Viva Pulse > Targeted Audience Surveys > Access setting > Off'. In the note specify selecting Everyone under Apply access settings to. Add: 'Custom user or group policies take precedence over the organisation-wide setting.' Keep the existing notice-path caveat; https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/control-access-admin-center documents the generic policy route and precedence.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaPulse -FeatureId <FeatureId> -Name <PolicyName> -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone creates a tenant-wide feature access policy.
claims.quote: The Everyone switch specifies that the policy applies to all users in the organization. ... $false: The feature is not enabled by the policy.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchange/add-vivamodulefeaturepolicy to sources, keeping the call and FeatureId discovery note. Clarify in the note: 'The Everyone policy is the tenant default; policies assigned to individual users or groups take precedence.' The existing https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/manage-access-policies page identifies VivaPulse as the Pulse ModuleID.

claims.claim: Get-VivaModuleFeature -ModuleId VivaPulse lists supported Viva Pulse features and their FeatureIds.
claims.quote: Pulse | VivaPulse ... Use the Get-VivaModuleFeature PowerShell cmdlet to get a list of all of the features available in a specific Microsoft 365 app and their associated IDs.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].note; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Viva Pulse admin controls targeted audience surveys through Viva feature access management.
claims.quote: This feature is on by default and is controlled by your Viva Pulse admin through Viva feature access management.

claims.claim: The minimum recipient setting is in Viva Pulse > Manage > Privacy > Minimum number of recipients and responses > Minimum recipients.
claims.quote: In the Manage tab, go to the Privacy tab. Under the Minimum number of recipients and responses heading go to the Minimum recipients section

claims.claim: The Viva Pulse admin role manages the in-app minimum recipient count.
claims.quote: The Viva Pulse in-app experience can be managed by users with the Viva Pulse admin role. ... You can manage all settings for the in-app Viva Pulse experience in the Manage tab.

claims.claim: The minimum recipient setting accepts values between 3 and 25.
claims.quote: The minimum value allowed is 3 and maximum value allowed is 25.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API for the Pulse minimum recipient count as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Pulse minimum recipients privacy setting API Microsoft Graph PowerShell minimum recipient count. Read results and opened set-up-in-app-pulse-experience, feature-access-management and manage-access-policies; no setting API found.

claims.claim: Learn's general feature access management table does not list Targeted Audience Surveys.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Pulse targeted audience surveys; read the full feature-access-management table. Its Pulse entries are Customization, Delegation, Team conversations, Copilot in Viva Pulse and Viva Pulse experience with Microsoft Copilot, not Targeted Audience Surveys.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice gives the alternative admin centre route Setup > Microsoft Viva > Feature access management > Viva Pulse.
claims.quote: Administrators can disable this feature in the Microsoft 365 admin center by navigating to Setup > Microsoft Viva > Feature access management > Viva Pulse and turning off Targeted Audience Surveys.

claims.claim: Learn's Copilot impact page gives Admin settings > Confidentiality for minimum recipients, differing from the cited in-app setup page's Manage > Privacy.
claims.quote: The audience must meet your organization's minimum recipient count, which your Viva Pulse admin sets under Admin settings > Confidentiality.

claims.claim: The AI Administrator manages the Viva Insights exclusion list.
claims.quote: Create a unified exclusion list for the Copilot Dashboard, Agent Dashboard, Consumption Dashboard, and Viva Insights (hide users from aggregates). Applies to: AI Administrator

claims.quote: Review who holds the CxO or CxO-delegate role ... and remove anyone who should not survey the whole Copilot population. Table controls: pre-built audience feature access; minimum recipient count.
claims.fix: Append to the role-review checklist item: 'Role-assignment management is not covered by the controls table.' Do not add a control row.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist instructs readers to check exclusion lists, but the controls table has no corresponding row.
claims.quote: Check that the Viva Insights exclusion list is current ... Re-check exclusion lists and role assignments after reorganisations ... The Viva Insights exclusion list ... is not a row here
claims.fix: Append to the exclusion-list checklist item: 'Exclusion-list management is not covered by the controls table.' Do not add a control row.
